# Amber Landing

<!-- passage:watch-002 -->
# East Weir

Watch 002

### Clear approach

Before a delivery arrives, walk the path from the landing to East Weir with both hands free. Mark places where the load requires a second person. A route may be suitable for a light meter and awkward for a bench case because of the turn at the rack. Move removable trip hazards away from the path and call maintenance for anything bolted down. Add the location of each temporary marker to the shift sketch.

### Store inventory

The stores clerk checks the back of each shelf at East Weir before ordering a replacement. The count includes tagged items waiting for inspection, with those items shown in a separate column from serviceable stock. Compare the actual quantity with the card rather than with the last invoice. If the clerks disagree, hold the line until someone reads the serials aloud. The weekly report records any supplement supplied by a neighboring store.

### Recorder conflict

When a stored minute at East Weir differs from a second export, compare the station address and the source revision before opening the value fields. Keep the recorded reading while the mismatch is investigated. An authorized replacement gets a paired entry citing the old value, the corrected value, and the reason for accepting it. Review the neighboring minutes after a change. A conflict list is useful even when the review leaves every stored number untouched.

### Paint and tags

Apply a replacement marker only after matching the number on the field sketch to the metal plate. Put the date at the foot of the marker where a fresh coat will leave it visible. The paint in the dry box at East Weir is suitable for the wood rail and some metal tabs. Inspect any enamel tag in daylight before covering it. A recorded abbreviation may mean a location on the sketch rather than a missing word.

### Supply route

The afternoon delivery uses the inland path when visitors fill the landing. The dispatch card names the carrier and the place to leave signed receipts for East Weir. Count both soft bags and hard cases before setting off. Give the storekeeper the complete set in one handoff if both staff members are available. If two trips are needed, note which portion moved on each trip so the destination can reconcile the count with the dispatch record.

### Agreement check

Once the measurements for the shift arrive, place the paper slips next to the official list. Compare station names and receive times first. Use the witness annotation if a number was read aloud and written by a second observer. Two values at East Weir may agree by rounding even though they differ in the original units. Record the original precision and repeat any comparison that lacks a confirmed reference. Keep the operator's note with the final accepted line.

### Water mark

Use the brass mark under the middle rung at East Weir as the local reference. Wipe the rail before lowering the staff. Record the raw height before converting to a chart datum, and keep the wet line out of the arithmetic when swell climbs over the staff. When the estimate is noisy, collect another observation from the protected side. The archived value preserves both the units written on the staff and the offset on the reference plate.

### Dispatch record

Pairs of observations can share the same minute without belonging to the same event. The dispatcher at East Weir compares the radio designation, the end of the message, and the point of origin. Open a separate entry for a second station reporting similar conditions. Corrections use the identifier from the original dispatch, with the new wording and the watch officer's initials below it. Duplicate reports from packet retries remain attached to the first entry.
<!-- passage:watch-003 -->
# Reed Crossing

Watch 003

### Feedback from the crossing

The boat crew reports conditions after rounding the last marker. Sketch the affected bank rather than guessing an angle from memory. If the watch at Reed Crossing requests another pass, repeat the same approach at the authorized speed and observe the outer buoy before the inner one. In the report, identify the reading made from the boat distinctly from the number watched later on the shore screen. The two readings may have different time bases.

### Pump inspection

Read the disconnect card before touching the case at Reed Crossing. Confirm the isolation steps with the second worker and note when the gauge settled. If the cabinet pressure is unclear, leave the cover in place and use the inspection window to describe the visible condition. Finish the report before returning the key. The field service lead records the planned recheck separately from approval to return the equipment to service.

### Lock and key

The watch key for Reed Crossing travels with the issue docket. Moving the key to the spare box changes the location recorded on the docket and leaves the watch owner unchanged. When a break means the owner cannot sign a handoff, the duty officer records a temporary custodian and checks the return time at the end of the shift. Cross out a mistaken entry with a single line and keep its original wording readable.

### Spare cells

Put cells coming off duty into the slotted return box and run the physical inspection before charging. Test a dry set before putting it into a handheld set. Printed charger capacity describes the tray, and the duty crew uses its charge indicator to decide when to return a cell to stock. At Reed Crossing, store candidates for recycling separately from known-good stock. A repair note includes the device that drew power and the approximate operating time.

### Watch handover

The outgoing observer at Reed Crossing reads the shift card aloud before leaving the platform. First distinguish conditions seen from warnings heard on the radio. The incoming watch initials each transfer and checks the rack keys against the pegboard. A handwritten time without a zone stays unresolved in the margin until the sender confirms the clock that produced it. Leave the next patrol a fresh card and attach the paper bearing the original correction.

### Sensor bracket

The hinged bracket at Reed Crossing is easiest to inspect while the platform is dry. Check the witness line on the upper bolt before testing the hinge. A bracket in good condition swings freely without losing its position when the pin seats. Leave the spring repair to the workshop if it binds under load. Record where the old sensor cable met the upright, because a replacement lead has a slightly different bend radius.

# Hazel Dock

Watch 005

### Inspection sequence

Check borrowed equipment in the order used on the trail. Retain the route ticket until all four cabinets have been closed.

4. At Hazel Dock, return the route ticket to the rack that issued it.

### Inspection sequence

Leave the original identifier on a relabeled bottle. The second card records the replacement tag and why it was needed.

The rack at North Reach has three A slots and one spare feed. Connect a test instrument to the spare feed during setup so the recorder on duty remains available. A plug that appears to fit can still carry the wrong signal, so compare the route label with the patch sheet before applying power. Return all caps to the loose-port basket. An unused labeled intake stays registered even while a spare feed takes its place.
